On arrival the sani bucket in the facility was observed at approximately 10 ppm CL. Effective concentrations for CL sanitizers is 50-200 ppm. The bucket was remade to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers are maintained at effective concentrations at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above.

On arrival the hot holding unit next to the rice cooker and window was observed to not be on with TCS foods inside. Chicken was probed and observed at 84F internal temperature. The unit was turned back on and the foods currently in it discarded. Ensure that all TCS foods are maintained at proper temperatures at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

An employee was observed to don gloves without hand washing. Hand washing should be taking place regularly and consistently during food operations, and specifically prior to donning gloves and when changing tasks. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to review hand washing procedures with employees to ensure safe practices are always taking place in the facility.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

A food handler was observed to wash their hands and use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted with both current workers. Ensure hand washing is completed correctly at all times, including using a clean barrier to turn off the faucet to protect the freshly cleaned hands from re-contamination.

findings.citation_text:

On arrival the PIC could not provide any form of verification that the employees were informed of their responsibility to report foodborne illness related symptoms and diagnosis. Blank copies of the SCDPH reporting agreements were found while searching for documentation and signed by the employees during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Maintain this documentation at the facility moving forward.

findings.citation_text:

findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 


Multiple locations in the building used for storage are observed with rodent droppings scattered about. No rodents are observed and no chewing is observed on any packaging at this time. Cleaning was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to clean up the droppings from the facility. If they notice more droppings appearing after the clean-up they should contact pest control for maintenance. findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.

2-301.15 Where to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK or APPROVED automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for FOOD preparation or WAREWASHING, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste. 

An employee was observed to wash their hands in the three part sink as they entered the unit after having lunch. Education was conduced with the PIC and they are instructed to review with all employees as applicable. Always wash hands correctly and in a designated hand sink.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
(REEPAT x2) 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. 

1) There are tears in the mesh door used for entering the unit by employees. 2) The roof grate has a mesh covering that has come loose and is no longer preventing pest entry. 3) The fan at the back wall of the unit in the corner away from the door is not functioning while the vent is open. These items are allowing for the entrance of pests and should be fixed. These items will be re-evaluated at the follow-up being scheduled in 10 days.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

1) Several flies of both the house and fruit/gnat variations are observed in the mobile unit while it is in operation. Several fly strips are observed in use at this time but do not appear to be sufficient for the current needs. 2) Several gnats/fruit flies are observed in the storage shed in the vicinity of the bags of onions. Both situations were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to remedy them prior to the follow-up. Ten days lands on a Saturday, therefore the follow-up is being scheduled for the following Monday.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

There was no water source available at the mobile unit. Without water service the employees could not have washed their hands at this location when entering the mobile unit nor at other times that hand washing would be required throughout operations. The facility was in the middle of cooking and there was food preparation that occurred prior to creation of the fried rice product.  Hand washing should be taking place regularly and consistently during food operations. During the inspection, the rice was discarded and operations halted while water was made available. The facility acknowledged that they were going to stay closed while the water was unavailable - so the importance of water availability was known, but the application was lacking. The facility was advised that when the water freezes and any instance where water is unavailable they should close.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.citation_text:
3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

It appears that food preparation is taking place in the storage shed next to the mobile unit. This location is only approved for use as dry storage and cannot be used for food preparation. This shall be evaluated again at the follow up in 10 days. Cease these operations moving forward unless approval is acquired. Approval would required renovations inside of the shed as this was previously discussed in the pre-opening inspection for the shed that no preparation was to occur in the space as no hand sink was available. Clean the top of the reach-in freezer where a knife and protein juices and vegetable remnants were observed. There is limited space within the mobile unit and the facility was warned against prepping in this space.

findings.citation_text:

(A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables.

Multiple items in the standing cooler (as you enter the unit) are observed stored in contact with or over items that allow for cross contamination prohibited by the Code. Items include: 1) raw chicken stored over broccoli; 2) shrimp over cooked noodles and; 3) raw scallops stored over carrots. Items were discussed with the PIC and instructed to store TCS foods correctly in the coolers. Items were not immediately moved. This will be one of the talking points to discuss with the Health Educator from SCDPH.

findings.comment:
4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

Multiple food items in the coolers are observed being stored in grocery bags. These are not approved or safe items for food storage. Ensure that food items are stored in safe and proper containers at all times. This shall be re-evaluated at the follow up in 10 days.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
findings.citation_text:
5-104.11 System. Water shall be received from the source through the use of: (A) An APPROVED public water main; or (B) One or more of the following that shall be constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW:  (1) Nonpublic water main, water pumps, pipes, hoses, connections, and other appurtenances, (2) Water transport vehicles, or (3) Water containers. 

On arrival there was no water service available in the unit and the unit is in operation. Water service was made available during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that potable water is available at all times that the facility is in operation. If water is not available the unit must close until water service is made available again.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11  The facility is using every inch of horizontal space to store equipment. There is virtually no flat counters available for preparation - thus the flat top of the reach-in freezer is being used in the storage shed. The facility would benefit from providing additional counter space by eliminating some equipment OR provided a washable, temporary, and flat surface to extend over the triple sink when not-in-use. The additional counter space is necessary for proper preparation of foods. Create more surface space for preparation processes. 


PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair and designed to accommodate the need and use of the type of operation occurring.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11(A) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection.

After review with the Department Head (CK) this violation is being awarded for the previous routine inspection conducted on 1/28/25. Several Priority and Priority Foundation violations were observed. A follow up is being set for one month to ensure training is taking place in the unit and food safety standards are being maintained at all times.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

An employee was observed to don gloves without hand washing. Education was conducted and they hands rewashed to correct. Ensure education takes place with staff to ensure hand washing takes place at all times that it is required.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

An employee did not use a clean barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. This recontaminated the hands prior to food handling. Education was conducted and the hands rewashed re-washed to correct. Ensure that hands are not immediately recontaminated after hand washing prior to food handling.

On arrival the hand sink in the facility is observed with multiple bowls and utensils in it, preventing use. The PIC removed the items without asking after the inspector stepped in. Ensure that the hand sinks are maintained accessible at all times to promote good hand washing practices.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.

6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

On arrival the hand sink in the mobile unit is without paper towels. When notified the PIC retrieved more from the shed and refilled the dispenser. Ensure that the hand sink has required supplies at all times.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Food Contact with Equipment and Utensils. FOOD shall only contact surfaces of: (A) EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned as specified under Part 4-6 of this Code and SANITIZED as specified under Part 4-7 of this Code.

While removing the container used for single service items (refer to line item #45) the container was shaken over the side of a large wok that was in the process of cooking noodles. A couple of contaminants were observed to fall from the container into the noodles. The contaminants and affected sections of the foods were discarded. Education was conducted and they PIC should ensure that contamination is prevented at all times that foods are stored, handled and prepared.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15(B) Cooling Methods. (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers in which FOOD is being cooled shall be: (1) Arranged in the EQUIPMENT to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls; and (2) Loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination as specified under Subparagraph 3-305.11(A)(2), during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the FOOD. 

A large tub of rice is observed cooling on top of the dorm cooler in the facility. Temperatures are observed between 96F and 106F. At this stage active cooling should a have already begun for the rice. The rice is also 4-6 inches deep in the full size bus tub. Education was conducted and the tub moved into the standing cooler to correct the immediate violation. It is highly suggested that smaller pans and shallower amounts of rice are used for those pans to facilitate good cooling moving forward.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used

Four hours at any temperature below 134F.

(G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

Food employees present have not completed food handler training. All staff working in the kitchen must complete food handler training.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. 
The operator of this Class I facility has yet to acquire the allergen certificate. See that allergen training is completed for all certified food managers.  
Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: 2-102.12: (No CFPM present during the start of the inspection. See that additional staff become CFPM. Discussed with Ming and head cook the need to get certified. Gave online options to operator. A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment: Raw meats observed stored above cooked noodles and vegetables in the cooler. Discussed appropriate storage order. Ref. 3-302.11 [P]

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Lack of managerial control observed, as demonstrated by the violations below. CORRECTED— Provided knowledge on each violation. Ensure staff are trained on food safety.
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  [Pf]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
No CFM present at time of inspection. CORRECTED— Upon request, staff called owner (who is a CFM). Owner arrived during inspection.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
No handwashing observed in the mobile unit, despite food employees changing tasks, leaving the mobile unit, etc. CORRECTED— Provided education and discussed with PIC.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Handwashing sink observed containing rice and other food debris. Handwashing sink may only be used for handwashing and no other purposes. CORRECTED— Provided education and discussed with PIC.
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.comment:
Mobile unit has been using an unpermitted shed (located near the mobile unit) to store an additional cooler and chest freezer. TCS foods must be stored in the mobile unit or a permitted commissary kitchen. Inspector will follow up in twenty (20) days.
3-201.11: (A)-(B) FOOD shall be obtained from APPROVED source. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Raw shrimp and chicken observed stored above cut vegetables and prepared noodles in the 2 door cooler. CORRECTED— Discussed proper storage with staff. All foods are prepared together on the flat top grill. Cooler rearranged to prevent cross contamination during storage.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Soiled knives observed stored on the knife bar. Discussed with PIC. Some utensils were discarded. Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Multiple TCS foods observed stored at room temperature: shell eggs, garlic butter, and white rice. CORRECTED— Provided education on food storage. Garlic butter and rice were voluntarily discarded. Staff indicated that the shell eggs had been removed from cold holding at 1PM, therefore shell eggs will be used or discarded by 5PM.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment:
Eggs observed stored on the counter at room temperature. Eggs had been removed from cooler at 1PM, and will be used or discarded at 5PM. A written Time as a Control policy must be created for any items that will be kept on the counter. Items kept on the counter must be used or discarded after 4 hours. Inspector will help write a policy as needed.
3-501.19: (A) If time without temperature used for public health control, written procedure approved by regulatory authority shall be available upon request. [Pf]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Shrimp observed thawing in a 5 gallon bucket of water on the floor of the mobile unit. Discussed proper thawing methods. Thaw foods under running water or under refrigeration. CORRECTED— Shrimp observed at ~36F, and moved under running water. Due to water storage constraints, frozen foods may need to be thawed under refrigeration.
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Mobile unit door is not self closing. Provide a self-closer for the door or screen with magnets.
6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Many containers in use throughout the kitchen are too large to fit in the three compartment sink. Cease use of containers that are too large to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized in the mobile unit’s three compartment sink.
4-301.12: (A) Sink with 3-compartments shall be provided for EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS. (B) Sinks shall be capable of accommodating the immersion of the largest piece of EQUIPMENT or UTENSIL. A machine or alternative option can be used. [Pf]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
No sanitizer prepared at time of inspection. CORRECTED— Upon request, sanitizer was prepared  to a concentration of 200ppm.
4-303.11: (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. [Pf]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
No Cl test strips available. CORRECTED— Test strips provided. Ensure they are available to measure sanitizer concentration levels.
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Soil accumulation observed throughout the mobile unit. Increase cleaning frequency to prevent soil accumulation. 
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
Water supply hose is not food grade. Replace hose with one that is approved for food/drinking use.
5-302.16: A hose used for conveying DRINKING WATER from a water tank shall be: (A) Safe; (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent;(C) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition; (D) Finished with a SMOOTH interior surface; (E) Clearly and durably identified as to its use if not permanently attached. [P]

findings.comment:

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]
